description: Below the 4 eV S(a,b) cutoff, O-16 and fuel are treated as 0K free-gas (target at rest, downscatter only). Add proper free-gas thermal-motion up-scatter kernel (OpenMC free_gas / DBRC) so non-H nuclei thermalize correctly. Currently H S(a,b) supplies all up-scatter. From op-6tz.12 review.
title: outram-mc: free-gas thermal target-motion for O-16/fuel below cutoff

acceptance_criteria: For a batch of particle states in a CSG pincell, GPU nearest-surface distance + crossed-surface id match CPU distance_to_boundary (f32 tolerance) for interior and near-boundary starts.
description: Per-particle nearest-crossing search on device: over the current cell's bounding surfaces take the minimum positive C1 distance and identify the crossed surface — GPU analog of geometry.rs distance_to_boundary (surface arm). Event-based, batch-resident.
title: outram-mc GPU: distance_to_boundary over general CSG (nearest-surface event)

description:
`outram_mc_libs::rng::lcg::prn` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs:26) does NOT reproduce OpenMC's `prn`.

Upstream (/home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:32-44):

    *seed = (prn_mult * (*seed) + prn_add);
    uint64_t word = ((*seed >> ((*seed >> 59u) + 5u)) ^ *seed) * 12605985483714917081ull;
    uint64_t result = (word >> 43u) ^ word;
    return ldexp(result, -64);

i.e. a PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation of the LCG state, scaled by 2^-64 (full 64-bit resolution).

Ours:

    *seed = seed.wrapping_mul(MULT).wrapping_add(INC);
    (*seed >> 12) as f64 * (1.0 / (1u64 << 52) as f64)

i.e. the raw top 52 bits of the state, no permutation. The doc comment claims 'Maps to double prn(uint64_t* seed) in OpenMC' — it does not.

MEASURED EVIDENCE (2026-08-06). From seed = 1, first five draws:
  ours:   0.423209170872713, 0.509407442883721, 0.648359393963430, 0.382863390508260, 0.795447749253532
  openmc: 0.710817359881671, 0.752996005805941, 0.330118988789542, 0.467186818550906, 0.046254968305997
The LCG STATE recurrence is identical on both sides (state after 5 draws = 0xCBA276B4B881A9F0 either way), so future_seed / jump-ahead / init_seed / the GPU integer-state mirror tests are all unaffected and remain correct. Only the state -> double output mapping diverges.

IMPACT. Our uniforms are a statistically reasonable generator (top bits of an LCG), so this is not a correctness catastrophe the way op-rbo was — but it does mean this crate can NEVER reproduce an OpenMC random sequence bit-for-bit, which undercuts the crate's stated purpose (CLAUDE.md: 'the crate's entire value is fidelity to OpenMC'). It also violates the mandatory porting rule: the current implementation is a re-derivation, not a port.

WHY NOT FIXED UNDER op-rbo (deliberate scoping decision, 2026-08-06). Blast radius is far larger than init_seed's:
  - every random number in the crate changes -> every k-eff, every V&V CSV, every openmc_notebook_comparison must be re-run;
  - the WGSL shaders (src/gpu/shaders/*, gpu::batched_flight / batched_event) derive their f32 uniform from the state with the port's formula and would need matching changes plus new GPU-vs-CPU mirror numbers;
  - crates/raffles consumes rng::lcg::prn directly (samplers.rs:315,437,541,1085) and its sampler outputs/recorded results would shift; that crate was explicitly out of bounds for the op-rbo agent.
This needs its own planned change with a full re-run of the crate's recorded statistics, not a drive-by.

ALSO NOTED while auditing rng/lcg.rs (no action taken):
  - future_seed matches upstream (random_lcg.cpp:91-120) exactly, including operation order. Verified.
  - MULT / INC / DEFAULT_STRIDE match prn_mult / prn_add / DEFAULT_STRIDE exactly. Verified.
  - NOT ported at all: future_prn (:50), advance_prn_seed (:82), init_particle_seeds (:70), and the N_STREAMS = 4 stream-index constants (random_lcg.h:12-16). init_particle_seeds in particular is the idiomatic upstream way to give one particle its four streams; callers here hand-roll it. Consider porting them for API parity.
  - Lcg64 is new work (an oorandom::Rand64 compat shim for boon-lay), not an OpenMC port; its rand_u64 returns the raw LCG state, whose low bits are weak. Fine as-is but should not be mistaken for an upstream-faithful API.
title: outram-mc-libs: rng::lcg::prn omits OpenMC's PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation
